strongest_angle: Examine the November 2026 American Geophysical Union study showing that planting native Polylepis trees in the wrong parts of the Andes reduces aquifer recharge and steals water from downstream communities.

key_facts.fact: Human actions have reduced Polylepis forests, the world's highest-elevation tropical trees, down to less than 10% of their original area in Peru, according to a November 2026 American Geophysical Union study.

A study published in October 2026 in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences by researchers including Jasper Oshun and Margaret M. Lang found that replacing grasslands with Polylepis forests in the seasonally dry Andes reduces aquifer recharge.

In Peru, large-scale tree-planting efforts are underway to restore Polylepis forests, which currently occupy less than 10% of their original historical range according to the American Geophysical Union.
